title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Despite having lost the source of his religious and political power, Sulyvahn, still wearing his torn robes from the battle, remained in the city's cathedral. The Pontiff set about bringing his knights back to life through necromancy, and had them patrol lower Irithyll as frigid spirits. In addition, his beasts regained control over access to the city and cornered Archdeacon McDonnell, who was leading Aldrich's legion, into the Water Reserve, implying his resolve to bring the city back under his control while Aldrich was still busy digesting Gwyndolin.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his complete domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. In response, Pontiff Sulyvahn seems to have exiled Aldrich to the Cathedral of the Deep, which specialized in rituals of purification from "stagnant darkness", in hopes that the sacred and serene waters of the Cathedral would contain Aldrich's dark habit. The Pontiff also gave one of his small dolls to Aldrich, in the event that he recovered to a point where he could return home.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: With great foresight and manipulation, Sulyvahn began his rise to power within Irithyll: the sorcerer used the Profaned Flame to enthrall the city's holy knights, corrupting their hearts with the unquenchable version of the Fire they venerated. His influence expanded also to the troops they commanded who became Sulyvahn's personal knights, reporting directly to him, acting as his watchful eyes first and as his designated killers second, effectively becoming his private militia and secret police. Those who were once holy knights became "fire witches" who carried the Profaned Flame of Sulyvahn on Immolation Tinders, also catalysts for the sorcery once so abhorred by the clergy, while the swords of the soldiers they led were imbued with the frost magic of their leader.

title: Pontiff Knight
snippet: When Pontiff Sulyvahn plotted to control Irithyll, he corrupted their leaders thanks to the unquenchable Profaned Flame that he found in the ruins of the Profaned Capital. After turning the captains of the army of Irithyll into sorcerers in his service, Sulyvahn also influenced the knights they led, gifting them golden crowns as they helped him seize power. After he took power, the knights would serve as Sulyvahn's watchful eyes and punitive blades. When Aldrich and his Deacons attacked Irithyll, the Pontiff Knights were all slain, and now they are frigid spirits brought back to life by the Pontiff's necromancy. Their swords are now gnawed by the insects of the deep spawned by the Evangelists, and the knights continuously spit dark souls as their bodies were hit and filled by the sorceries of the deacons.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
With Pontiff Sulyvahn relinquishing Gwyndolin, the Saint of the Deep was triumphant, taking up residence in the old Cathedral and beginning to feast on the old god. He would fall into a deep slumber in the process of consuming Gwyndolin, during which he would dream and perceive the form of a young, pale girl in hiding. The Aldrich Faithful guarded the old Cathedral to ward off any intrusion on Aldrich's slumber, with the ancient Silver Knights unwittingly aiding the consumption of their former master.

When the Ashen One seeking the Lords of Cinder arrives at Irithyll to slay Aldrich in their quest, he awakens to defend himself, puppeteering Gwyndolin's magic and body, as well as using a miracle developed from his dreams.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Having gained power in Irithyll, Sulyvahn set about cleansing the city of potential enemies, exiling or killing the Blades of the Darkmoon until there were no more knights in the order, eliminating the Painting Guardians, and even turning the Giants who worked in the city into slaves. The Pontiff would also build an immense dungeon underground near the Profaned Capital, employing its survivors as cruel jailers in his service, and building prisons for humans around the oldest cell of a giant. In addition, Sulyvahn erected a magic barrier around Irithyll to prevent anyone from entering or leaving without his permission, giving special dolls to his most valued subjects to move through it freely, an artifact which reminded them ceaselessly that their "home" would always be the Boreal Valley. title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: When Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Emma, the High Priestess of Lothric, would send out messengers bearing the banner of Lothric to ask allied countries for aid in resolving their internal situation. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

 theories : It is possible to theorize that the manor at the outskirts of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley was the house that was granted to Sulyvahn when he was accepted into the society of the nobles. The original description of the bonfire is "Abandoned House on the Outskirts of the City” (街はずれの廃屋)", implying that the Manor was built on the edge of the city as its inhabitant was not equal to the other nobles of divine origins, and that it had become abandoned by the time that Sulyvahn would have ascended to Pontiff. Furthermore, the "Distant Manor" bonfire is en route to the Irithyll Dungeon and consequently the Profaned Capital, where Sulyvahn would find the Profaned Flame below Irithyll, making the access under his house a logical point along his discovery. Curiously, the manor is also the place where the city's sewage system dumped its waste.

snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:

The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn is extremely susceptible to parrying, each riposte dealing upwards of 1000 damage. A couple of his moves can be easily exploited as the swings of his flaming sword are usually telegraphed and can be predicted. Utilizing parry and riposte throughout the battle can end the fight quickly, leaving him close to death just as he begins to summon the phantom.

An easier method that forgoes parries (and even rolling) is to simply circle around him clockwise while raising a shield that offers 100% physical absorption. Circling left (Sulyvahn's right) will avoid almost every attack and allow you time to land one or two hits after most of his attack patterns. When he begins to summon a phantom, start attacking immediately to kill the phantom as quick as possible and resume circling clockwise. Since this strategy allows you to steadily attack throughout the fight, it will typically end before he tries to summon another one.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Even after the awakening of the Ashen One, the influence of several gods or their descendants is still present in the world.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin, once the king of the gods and of Irithyll, had been imprisoned in the city's old cathedral by Pontiff Sulyvahn, that stripped him of his power to rule in his place. However Aldrich, Devourer of Gods had arrived in Irithyll and, after defeating Sulyvahn, he began to devour Gwyndolin. Yorshka, Gwyndolin'sister, is still alive and leads the knights's of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant, but she has been imprisoned by Sulyvahn in an isolated tower.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At his new posting at the Cathedral, Aldrich was provided a steady flow of sustenance in the form of the Road of Sacrifices. The Cathedral would dispatch Evangelists to establish missions and gain influence at the Undead Settlement; these preachers would tell stories of enlightenment to the cursed Undead, who were shipped off en masse to become feed to Aldrich's gluttony. At some point, he would desire for others to share in the elation of devouring men; to this end he fashioned warped magic rings that allowed one to feel the same depraved sensations as the repulsive maneater. The bearers of these rings underwent a mutation similar to his, transforming into bestial creatures with stomachs filled with the remains of their meals and infused with the power of the Deep.

title: The Deep
snippet: The Deep, as it is encountered in *Dark Souls III*, is likely a corruption of a gentler, more serene "Deep Sea", which was once employed by Way of White clerics in the Cathedral of the Deep for purification purposes. The quietude of the Deep was seemingly disturbed with the arrival of Aldrich, a Way of White cleric hailing from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. At his home, Aldrich had engaged in grotesque behaviour that presumably alarmed Pontiff Sulyvahn, the leader of the Way of White faith in the city, who decided on posting him at the Cathedral of the Deep— perhaps in hopes that he could benefit from the Cathedral's services to cleanse himself. It seems, however, that the stay of Aldrich was concurrent with the rapid degeneration of the Cathedral and its pond, to which Aldrich presumably contributed greatly.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beasts can be staggered. If their head is struck with enough damage, it will cause them to rear back and expose their chest for a critical attack. If this attack fails to kill them, it will knock them down onto their back, causing them to flail about for a period of time before being rendered helpless to be finished off. However, if a single attack does not kill them while they are in this state, they will get back up and resume the fight, though they can still be killed before their recovery animation completes.

During its lightning attack, it is advised to hug their chest or their sides. The attack is telegraphed and is rather easy to avoid as it affects a limited area and does not track the target, giving the player time to heal or attack without retaliation.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich is most vulnerable on his tail, which provides an area where the player may attack without risking themselves too much from being in the staff's range.

Upon receiving some damage, Aldrich will raise his staff and create a big vortex on the ground in front of him, plunging inside to escape from punishment. This vortex is heavily damaging and the player would be wise in not attacking the boss too many times in a row, preparing instead to move away when it is cast. Aldrich will emerge a moment later on the other side of the hall, as far away from the player as possible, trying to buy some time to cast more spells.

Once Aldrich has lost about 40% of his health, he will buff his scythe with fire. At this point, every time he emerges from the ground, he will deal damage to nearby players while a much greater amount of homing projectiles spawn with him as he rises.

snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their humanity, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

The only survivors of the Capital are the Handmaids, the court sorcerer Eamon, and the four malformed women. The Handmaids who served in the Capital reportedly took pleasure in hurting others.

Sometime after the Profaned Flame destroyed the Capital, Pontiff Sulyvahn discovered the Profaned Flame and the Capital, "a burning ambition took root within him". He would later infuse the Profaned Flame within his own greatsword, and would perhaps introduce the Profaned Flame to the Fire Witches. They would learn to use its power and summon firestorms with their halberds., and would eventually take Irithyll for themselves.

Sulyvahn would later build a dungeon, and hired some handmaids to guard the prison, which preserves part of the profaned flame in a icy skull.

title: The Deep
snippet: At his new posting at the Cathedral, Aldrich was provided a steady flow of sustenance in the form of the Road of Sacrifices. The Cathedral would dispatch Evangelists to establish missions and gain influence at the Undead Settlement; these preachers would tell stories of enlightenment to the cursed Undead, who were shipped off en masse to become feed to Aldrich's gluttony. At some point, he would desire for others to share in the elation of devouring men; to this end he fashioned warped magic rings that allowed one to feel the same depraved sensations as the repulsive maneater. The bearers of these rings mutated into accursed bestial creatures with stomachs filled with the remains of their meals.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
With Elfriede at the helm, the Sable Church developed dark miracles, forged specialized weaponry, and trained knights unflinchingly loyal to their cause. The influence of the Sable Church would extend beyond Londor and into other realms via Londor Pale Shades, assassins and knights who served the interests of the Church abroad. At some point, Sir Vilhelm would come under the employ of the three sisters of the Church. He was especially loyal to Elfriede, becoming her steadfast follower and cold-blooded hangman.

Elfriede eventually departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, realizing Kaathe's vision of an Age of Dark, or wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose. Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash.

title: Way of White
snippet: After nearly all of the deities had abandoned Anor Londo, Lloyd moved his seat of power to the region of Thorolund, which then became the cultural and political center of the Way of White. The god had absolute power over the country and thus chose among the nobles of the region the ones who would become his apostles and high priests of the Way of White, gifting them holy rings to increase their magic and making their duty the protection of law and social classes. In addition, Thorolund's clerics showed off their rank with their robes and those of high rank obtained talismans that worked even without faith but thanks to Lloyd's divine protection.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. By this time, the notion that Hollows were the "true face of man" had become more accepted, propagated especially by the Pilgrims of Londor, melding the two titles of Dark Lord into

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn ordered the Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight, equivalent to being exiled. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given the eye rings of the Pontiff, which eventually transformed them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, which ensured Sulyvahn's total control over the knights and deprived them of any means of desertion.

The Dancer was sent to Lothric together with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma. Like other Outrider Knights, she would end up transformed into a frenzied beast by the rings of the Pontiff, causing her armor to be fused with her hide.

title: The Deep
snippet:
It is unclear what would have become of Aldrich at the end of the Age of Fire. While the champion of the Deep has already been defeated when the Ashen One visits the Ringed City or the Dreg Heap, it seems that his visions of an incoming Age of Deep Sea were close to coming to pass, with the remnants of the world of Man bustling with the sunken, stagnated dregs of humanity, the malformed legacy of the Dark Soul which had been suppressed by the Darksign for millennia.

To prevent the advent of the Age of Deep following the weakening of the First Flame, the plan of the Sable Church of Londor has become to tear the Flame off its Kiln and preserve it within a Lord of Hollows who can exploit its power, freezing the state of the world thanks to their Dark Sigil.

title: Gods
snippet:
Havel the Rock, a battlefield compatriot of Gwyn who fought at his side against the Everlasting Dragons and inspired many warriors who wore similar equipment. He is referred to as a "bishop" , and is clearly part of the faith of the Way of White, as there were even "priests of Havel" and miracles recalling his tales, although whether he was actually deified, or part of Gwyn's species, is unclear.
Seath, an Everlasting Dragon who sided with Gwyn against his own species. After the war, he was granted Dukedom, married a woman in Gwyn's family, and came to be regarded as the Godfather of sorcery, although he was seemingly not deified.
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: After nearly all of the deities had abandoned Anor Londo, Lloyd moved his seat of power to a region in the world of men which would become known as Thorolund, acting as the political center of his new Way of White. The god held absolute power over the country and chose his apostles among the nobility, gifting holy rings that enanched magic to those of them who would become high priests of the Way of White, making their duty the protection of law and social classes.

title: Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon
snippet:
However, Sir Yorgh and his powerful Drakeblood Knights eventually mounted a siege and invaded Shulva in order to defeat the dragon and steal its fresh blood, which they believed granted "a true understanding of life". They were able to defeat all the guards of Dragon's Sanctum and attack Dragon's Rest where Yorgh engaged Sinh. The dragon proved far too powerful for Yorgh to withstand, and he was killed as the poison which built up inside Sinh over the ages was expelled and completely wiped out Sanctum City, covering it in toxic poison. Yorgh's body lies near the dragon's nest, holding Yorgh's Ring.

It is unknown whether this poison was also the cause of the contamination of Black Gulch, but its proximity to Shulva and noxious nature of Black Gulch may have some connection.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Some of the dethroned god's followers, now cast out from the reformed faith, would find refuge in the Painted World of Ariandel, bringing with them the lost miracles of the old religion and fully believing that one day the aureoles of light associated with Lloyd would return with him. It's possible that Slave Knight Gael was once such a believer, due to his usage of that very miracle. That is in spite of his nature as a cursed Undead, which the old god seemingly despised.

title: Lindelt
snippet: Thanks to their well-honed miracles and unwavering faith in the face of death, the cleric knights of the Archdrake Church were a formidable force on the battlefield, even managing to stand up to the army of King Vendrick as worthy rivals. Miracles like Replenishment and Resplendent Life allowed the knights to endure and heal from arduous battles. Among the high-ranked clerics, Forsalle stood out thanks to his mastery of miracles, and led many battles across his country's borders. He earned the title of "holy knight" and was feared for his "demonic power" by his enemies. However, some cleric knights of Lindelt defected to escape their country's authoritarian rule. These clerics tried to start new lives in the destroyed kingdom of Drangleic and found their way inside the Shrine of Amana, where some of them went hollow.

title: The Deep
snippet: Over time the deacons themselves began to succumb to the Deep. Some of those who slipped into the Deep began to wallow in this filth, while others were steadfast and resisted the maddening corruption to some meaningful degree, though they still began to practice dark arts. They added stories of the Deep to the scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and created sorceries that manipulated dark soul dregs, which he imparted to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons. The deacons' faith in the gods was irreversibly corroded, and they began to worship the Deep and its powerful entity: Aldrich, the "Saint of the Deep".

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Before the Lord of Sunlight sacrificed himself to link the First Flame, he divided his power among his family, instructed his sons to lead humanity and passed down his sunlight and title to his firstborn. However, his son would eventually be exiled and erased from history due to his actions, and taking advantage of the situation, Lloyd would proclaim himself "Allfather", leader of all the other gods and main figure of the Way of White. His claim remained unopposed, despite his grandnephew Gwyndolin having a stronger case for inheriting the position seeing as it was the religion of Gwyn's immediate family. Sadly, the reclusive god still viewed himself as repulsive and unworthy of his father's legacy and the task he had bestowed upon him.

title: Drangleic
snippet: While Drangleic prospered under Vendrick, the king's older brother Aldia never took an interest in the political affairs of the kingdom he had helped found, preferring to remain in his mansion and dedicating himself to the research of the truths of the world. His keep attracted the greatest minds of the kingdom, who were keen to help with his studies and strange rituals. However, his research, motivated by a boundless desire to understand life, eventually took a dark turn, leading him to create blasphemous spells with a will of their own that chased their enemies, a characteristic of the Dark. He also created excessively destructive pyromancies just to test the limits of the Chaos flame through rituals, along with sorceries that augmented the magic imbued in a body well beyond their limits, damaging the life of the caster.

title: Gods
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.
King Oceiros, the King of Lothric who married Gwynevere. It is unknown what his original species was, but he would later become similar to a hybrid in an attempt to turn into a Dragon. He is the father of at least three of Gwynevere's children: Lorian, Lothric (named after the kingdom) and her youngest, Ocelotte, none of whom were deified; it is unclear whether or not he fathered Rosaria, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, or Gertrude, but as Lorian was the heir to the throne, he was likely the two's oldest son, and perhaps their oldest child together.

During the founding of the kingdom, the soldiers of Lothric had found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. And so these armors of Lothric's first knights were crafted: heavy masses of iron capable of withstanding dragon fire, similar in design to the ancient armor of the dragonslayers of Anor Londo, with their shields capable of absorbing the lightning breath of wyverns.

title: The Deep
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Aldrich denounced this call to action based on an epiphany: that an **Age of Deep** would soon be cast upon the world. The Cathedral had by then become a shrine to unspeakable horrors, to all repulsive rejects that once sought a cure in its cleansing waters. Within the Cathedral—in McDonnell's sorceries, and their taboo miracles— Aldrich observed a stagnation that seemed inherent to the world, belike rotten remains which find their way down into a dark, deep seabed. Following these ruminations on the nature of existence, Aldrich concluded that an Age of Deep was what followed the waning Age of Fire. He understood that all things would stagnate into the Deep, including the representatives of the old world order; he also understood that he was in a position where he could help usher in the new Age. Thus he set out to

title: The Deep
snippet: In a world defined by the Deep Sea, human dregs that sink to the lowest possible depths become the basis of everything; and, as envisioned by Aldrich, a "deep sea" engulfs the world in rotten, putrid darkness. These dark soul dregs, having stewed for ages in the depths, would also possess what remains of humans, enveloping them in the dark dampness of the Deep. Consequently, in the midst of a world covered in stagnant slime, the condition of the human race would become that of murky humanoid beings possessed by stewed or rebellious dark souls, capable of channelling the Deep to cast dark sorceries and instill their weapons. In addition, the Depths would have continued to generate parasitic and hungry larvae and insects that would plague humans.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. He spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. The Cathedral, once a peaceful and sacred place for purification, was corrupted by the foul Aldrich, as darkness stagnated and accumulated in the Deep until it had become the final rest of abhorrent creatures. Archdeacon McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. McDonnell spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. In time the cathedral's deacons became both clergymen and sorcerers, embracing the cult of the Deep. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
When he rears up and aims his bow, he will launch an expanding wave of highly damaging arrows in front of him, allowing you to circle behind him and get hits in.

Throughout the course of the battle, Aldrich will be constantly summoning small homing projectiles. Each one of these, on its own, only deals a small amount of damage and the player may even opt to sustain a few of them in exchange of inflicting some damage to the boss. However, if they are caught by the full attack, they will sustain heavy damage, which may even kill them in a single barrage.

Aldrich is most vulnerable on his tail, which provides an area where the player may attack without risking themselves too much from being in the staff's range.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : At the beginning of the fight, charge at Aldrich to avoid his hard-hitting soul spear. Get behind him and focus your attacks on his tail. This leaves him with nothing to do but swing his two slow, devastating melee attacks or teleport across the room (usually, adjacent to where he teleported from).

At about 55%-60% health, he will teleport and come back up, buffed with fire. His arrows also go from going forward to following a specific player. If the arrows following the player catch up to them, then that player will most likely go down quick. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended for this fight.

Casting the sorcery Twisted Wall of Light can negate Aldrich's ranged attacks, including his arrow barrage in the second phase, allowing one to wait out the attack by casting repeatedly.

snippet:
If the player is killed whilst in darkened Anor Londo, they are returned to the first bonfire regardless of whether they have rested there or not. Whether it is a glitch or an intended function by the developers is unconfirmed.

If the player desires to fight Dark Sun Gwyndolin via an easy return to the boss area, it is preferable to either:
Leave Gwynevere alive so as to not make Anor Londo dark, and then fight Gwyndolin. This allows the player to respawn at the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire.
After killing Gwynevere, ignore the Darkmoon Knightess (so as not to kill her in combat) to keep the first Bonfire lit so that the player may warp to the Darkmoon Tomb after death.

If the player has already darkened Anor Londo and killed the Darkmoon Knightess, the fastest method will be to run to the entrance way of The Duke's Archives (only accessible after placing the Lordvessel) and using the bonfire by the elevator to warp.

 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

With strong scaling in Dexterity and respectable scaling in Strength, the Irithyll Rapier caters primarily to quality builds, and its moveset makes it a particular threat when wielded in the off-hand.
As well, it is the only thrusting sword with an innate status buildup, inflicting Frost with each hit. This, combined with its Shield Splitter skill, makes it particularly dangerous against enemies that wield shields, since not only can it proc Frostbite through the shield to debuff stamina recovery, but the skill can be used to break through the shield altogether.

The only drawbacks of this weapon are its average reach, tied with most other thrusting swords, and its inability to be infused, restricting its use to quality and Dexterity-focused builds.
